court: High Court of Judicature at Madras

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: N.Ponni and Minor Athi Krishna (rep. through his mother N.Ponni)

facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who got married in 2009. The wife filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(ia) of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court allowed the petition and dissolved the marriage. The wife also filed an application for restitution of conjugal rights under Section 9 of Hindu Marriage Act which was dismissed by the trial court.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's refusal to cohabit without a valid reason can be considered cruelty.
legal_principles.held: Though the appellant refused to come and did not relent from her demand for a separate matrimonial home, it is held that such refusal can be considered as cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse's demand for a separate matrimonial home can be considered as cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The appellant's demand for a separate matrimonial home and her refusal to come back unless the respondent agreed to set up an independent matrimonial home, it is held that such demand can be considered as cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The final order is to set aside the order made in H.M.O.P.No.320 and 426 of 2014 on the file of the Family Court, Madurai dated 11.11.2016.
